```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(palmerpenguins)
```

## What if someone could use your R function without RStudio?

**That's what `plumber` helps us do!**

![](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/lter_penguins.png){width="55%" fig-alt="Illustrations of penguin species"}

::: {.notes}
(0:00–0:35) We have been learning to write functions in R. Today I'll show how plumber lets other people use our functions through a web address.
:::

---

## What is `plumber`?

`plumber` is an R package that turns an **R function** into an **API**.

**An API lets one program ask another program for information.**

::: {.fragment}
**Ask through a URL → R calculates → Get an answer**
:::

::: {.notes}
(0:35–1:15) Think of an API as a way to ask a question. We send a request, R runs a function, and we get an answer back.
:::

---

## Let's use real penguin data

The `palmerpenguins` dataset contains measurements of **Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo** penguins.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(avg_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(species, avg_mass, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Average body mass (g)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18)
```

::: {.notes}
(1:15–2:00) This is real penguin data. The chart compares average body mass. Now imagine asking for the statistics of one species through a URL.
:::

---

## Turning an R Function into an API

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#* @get /penguins
function(species = "Adelie") {
  penguins |>
    filter(.data$species == .env$species) |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      avg_mass = round(mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      avg_flipper = round(mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
    )
}
```

::: {.fragment}
**The key:** `#* @get /penguins` makes this function accessible through a URL.
:::

::: {.fragment}
After adding the Plumber annotation, use `pr()` and `pr_run()` to start the API server and generate an interactive Swagger interface.
:::

::: {.notes}
(2:00–2:35) The new thing is the annotation. It tells plumber to create a web endpoint named penguins.
:::

## Why is this useful?

- Share results with people who don't use R.
- Let a website request statistics from R.
- Make predictions from an R model available to other apps.

**Takeaway: `plumber` lets us share what our R functions can do.**

<small>Sources: [plumber](https://www.rplumber.io/) · [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/)</small>

::: {.notes}
(4:05–4:40) Plumber is useful because you can write your analysis once and let other programs request the results. Thank you!
:::
